body:
Already fixed.
Sorry about missing that, it would appear my git pre commit hooks are outdated. Been a while since I had enough time to upstream something.
I'm not sure this is a good idea, as said in comment, this idea was previously rejected, and preference was for a separate server function.

Yeah, but most of the relevant logic for prev_transform management happens in `RenderForwardClustered::GeometryInstanceForwardClustered::set_transform`, which is directly called by `instance_set_transform`.

And that function is already tiny, so I see no point in splitting it up into two functions with either duplicated code or turning it into a wrapper around yet another function (which can then also be called by a hypothetical `teleport` function). And we already have way too many wrapper functions in the rendering logic imo.

Besides, teleportation is a feature with minor code changes that is most likely only going the be used in specific edge cases, so I would argue that a default parameter is the perfect solution for that.

I will try to bring this up at today's rendering meeting and ask for their opinion.

The issue mentioned before is referring to the command queue. Ideally we want to reduce as much as possible traffic between scene side and the servers, because all these commands have to be stored to be processed later (assuming not using single threaded).

`instance_set_transform()` is a pretty hot function, it may end up getting called tens of thousands of times in a frame. Having the machinery to store 10,000 unnecessary bools in the queue is a cost, that might be say 1000,000 or more bools crossing the queue per second, totally unnecessarily.

If it were a simple c++ function with no queue in between client and server, and the ability to inline / optimize etc, then I would be in agreement.

Wrappers on the server side on the other hand will be fully optimized by the compiler, there's no problem having a `reset` function grab the instance, and call `set_transform(xform, true)` internally (if that's the simplest way to implement it your side).

If it's any consolation, I started on early implementations of the physics interpolation with the exact function as you are using here, but we later realized it wasn't such a good idea, both in terms of compatibility and performance.

Should be fixed in the new version.

```suggestion
				Resets motion vectors and other interpolated values. Use this [i]after[/i] teleporting a mesh from a position to another to avoid ghosting artifacts.
```

This should probably more sensibly hook in with the existing `multimesh_instance_reset_physics_interpolation()` on line 494. The current transform should already be available in the server if required. When physics interpolation is in use, the (interpolated) transform won't be available anyway scene side.

_(`Multimeshes` are not changed in the new `SceneTreeFTI` BTW as there are no pressing reasons to move the multimesh instances scene side.)_

The naming isn't ideal currently, but we don't want to be calling two separate server functions here to do the same thing. If necessary we can consider renaming in a followup but it would be compat breaking.

Still not sure this name is good. With the `SceneTreeFTI`, this command will (currently anyway) no longer have any effect on the interpolation in the server. But that could change in the future, and this naming has to be future proof.

We keep going around in circles here, but ultimately imo it needs something generic that describes the intention and _NOT_ the functionality (as I say, like `instance_teleport`).
